From: Michelle Tan <michelle.tan@plumesys.com>

Cc: devops@plumesys.com, contracts@plumesys.com
Date: 2027-06-27 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff — onprem VPC attachment and topology for Plume pilot

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for taking this on. We're kicking off a pilot to host Redwood's private runtime inside our colocation racks. Primary asks for the initial review:

- Confirm control plane placement options (customer-controlled control plane vs. Redwood-managed in a VPC endpoint).
- Data plane routing and egress constraints (we need to prove tenant isolation and predictable egress).
- Minimal acceptance checklist for cutover to staging (firewall ports, NAT, MTU, BGP peering expectations).

Attached is our current network diagram (plume-network-diagram-v1.pdf) and a short list of compliance constraints from our security team.

Can we get a short architecture readout and a list of actions by Wednesday next week? Also request a short on-site or video walkthrough — our DevOps lead (DevOps Team) will join.

Thanks,
Michelle Tan
Head of Infrastructure
Plume Systems

Attachments: plume-network-diagram-v1.pdf (diagram, 1 page)
From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Michelle Tan <michelle.tan@plumesys.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-27 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff — onprem VPC attachment and topology for Plume pilot

Michelle —

Appreciate the diagram and constraint list. High-level summary below; I'll follow up with an annotated reference diagram and an acceptance checklist this afternoon.

Short answers up front:
- Control plane: we recommend Redwood-managed control plane into a customer VPC peering/privatelink for the first pilot (reduces operational overhead). Alternative: customer-hosted control plane (we provide the control-plane bundle) if Plume requires full control and air-gap.
- Data plane: runtime nodes (in Pod/VM form) will sit in your tenant VLANs; egress must be controlled via your NAT/egress gateways. We will require a small set of egress IPs for telemetry and license checks — listed in the acceptance checklist.
- Isolation: KV cache + model-weight storage will be mounted on ephemeral local disks; we recommend using SR-IOV or dedicated NICs for deterministic latency.

Action items I will deliver today:
1) Annotated reference diagram showing control/data plane placement (redwood-reference-controlplane-dataplane-v2.pdf).
2) Staging cutover acceptance checklist (ports, MTU, BGP snippets).
3) Quick canary plan for traffic routing and fallback.

Proposed times for a live walkthrough:
- Tue 2027-06-29 10:00 PT (30m)
- Wed 2027-06-30 14:00 PT (30m)

Which works for your DevOps lead?

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-reference-controlplane-dataplane-v2.pdf (2 pages)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-28 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff — onprem VPC attachment and topology for Plume pilot

Adding a few operational notes from the runtime team:

- Control-plane HA: if Plume opts for the Redwood-managed control plane, we run it across two AZs (or two colo pods) with keepalive and leader election. For on-prem single-pod pilots we add an additional standby in the Redwood control region to prevent split-brain.
- KV cache boundary: we strongly prefer keeping KV cache behind host-level network segmentation; exposing it across customer networks increases attack surface.
- Observability: telemetry uses a push model to the Redwood collector on port 443; we can support an internal collector if Plume requires traffic to stay on-prem.

Questions for Plume before the walkthrough:
1) Do you have an internal certificate authority for mTLS between control/data components or do you want Redwood to provide certs?
2) Are you able to reserve two /28s for routing and health-check egress (one for runtime egress, one for collector/telemetry)?
3) Preferred failover behavior: immediate fallback to Redwood-hosted model variant, or pause requests until on-prem recovers?

I've attached a segmentation spreadsheet to drive the conversation and map ports to owners (segmentation-matrix.xlsx).

—Jonas
Principal Infra Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: segmentation-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Michelle Tan <michelle.tan@plumesys.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: devops@plumesys.com, contracts@plumesys.com, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-28 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff — onprem VPC attachment and topology for Plume pilot

Thanks Mateo and Jonas —

This looks good. Quick answers:
- We have an internal CA and prefer to use our PKI for mTLS; we'll export the intermediate certs for the handshake.
- We can reserve two /28s; I'll have network ops carve them out before the walkthrough.
- For failover behavior, we prefer a brief pause (30s timeout) with automatic retry to the on-prem runtime — that keeps logs consistent for compliance. If on-prem is down for >15 minutes, automatically failover to Redwood-hosted model variant.

We'll take the walkthrough on Tue 2027-06-29 10:00 PT. DevOps will join: DevOps Team.

Please send calendar invite and a short pre-read that calls out the acceptance checklist and the certificate exchange steps.

Michelle Tan
Head of Infrastructure
Plume Systems
